# What Airtable personal access tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves
# alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: the identifier is the front of that run behind the three
# letters pat, which brings it to the seventeen characters an Airtable ID is,
# and the secret behind the dot is the run four times over, which is
# sixty-four hexadecimal characters. A token comes to eighty-two.

patterns: airtable-personal-access-token

# The one shape Airtable writes a token in. There is a single kind of string here
# rather than a table of them: a token carries no mark saying what it was scoped
# to or which bases it reaches, so the cases below are that one shape in the
# places a token is written. The first two are Airtable's own — its JavaScript
# client reads a token out of AIRTABLE_API_KEY and sends it as a bearer token.

case:     a token in the environment assignment the client reads
in:       AIRTABLE_API_KEY=pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      AIRTABLE_API_KEY=«airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     a token in the header a request carries it in
in:       Authorization: Bearer pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      Authorization: Bearer «airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     a token on a command line
in:       curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef' https://api.airtable.com/v0/meta/whoami
out:      curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer «airtable-personal-access-token»' https://api.airtable.com/v0/meta/whoami

case:     a token in json
in:       {"personalAccessToken":"pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
out:      {"personalAccessToken":"«airtable-personal-access-token»"}

case:     a token in a log line
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" token=pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" token=«airtable-personal-access-token»

# The dot between the identifier and the secret. It belongs to neither alphabet,
# which is what ends the identifier where it stands and what makes the count on
# either side of it readable at all. Written as anything else, or written twice,
# there is no token to find.

case:     a hyphen where the dot belongs
in:       pat0123456789abcd-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pat0123456789abcd-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     no separator at all
in:       pat0123456789abcd00123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pat0123456789abcd00123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a second dot written inside the secret
in:       pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The two counts either side of it. Fourteen characters finish the identifier
# and sixty-four are the secret, and both are read as counts rather than as
# floors. The identifier answers for either length by the dot moving: written
# shorter or longer, the dot no longer stands where a token's does and there is
# nothing to find. The secret has no such mark behind it, so a run longer than
# the count is a token and the characters written after it — which is the price
# of having no boundary behind the match, since a boundary there would drop this
# token rather than trim it and a real token written against a letter would come
# through whole.

case:     an identifier one character short
in:       pat0123456789abc.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pat0123456789abc.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an identifier one character long
in:       pat0123456789abcde.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pat0123456789abcde.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a secret one character short
in:       pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde

case:     a secret longer than the count is a token and what follows it
in:       pat0123456789abcd.01234567890123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «airtable-personal-access-token»6789abcdef

case:     a token followed by a dot and another sixty-four hexadecimal characters
in:       pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «airtable-personal-access-token».0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The alphabets the two halves are read in. The identifier is an Airtable ID, so
# it is letters and digits in either case; the secret is thirty-two bytes written
# in lowercase hexadecimal, and the other case is the widening the pattern's own
# file declines.

case:     an identifier written in both cases
in:       pat0123456789ABCD.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     an identifier drawn from the far end of the alphabet
in:       patZYXWVUzyxwvu98.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     an underscore in the identifier
in:       pat0123456789_bcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pat0123456789_bcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an uppercase secret
in:       pat0123456789abcd.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      pat0123456789abcd.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     one uppercase character in a secret
in:       pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdeF
out:      pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdeF

case:     a letter outside hexadecimal in the secret
in:       pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdefg123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdefg123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a character outside hexadecimal at the first character of the secret
in:       pat0123456789abcd.g123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pat0123456789abcd.g123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a space inside the identifier
in:       pat0123456789 bcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pat0123456789 bcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# What a token may be written against. The three letters and the dot are the
# whole of the anchor and there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token
# keeps its span whatever word character it abuts.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       AIRTABLE_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      AIRTABLE_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_«airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xpat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      x«airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     a word written against a token
in:       pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsuffix
out:      «airtable-personal-access-token»suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.
out:      the token is «airtable-personal-access-token».

case:     a multi-byte rune flush against the token on both sides
in:       日本語pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef日本語
out:      日本語«airtable-personal-access-token»日本語

case:     a token in a yaml value
in:       airtable:\n  token: pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      airtable:\n  token: «airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     a token in a query string
in:       https://api.airtable.com/v0/x?api_key=pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      https://api.airtable.com/v0/x?api_key=«airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     a token followed by a crlf
in:       AIRTABLE_API_KEY=pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\r\n
out:      AIRTABLE_API_KEY=«airtable-personal-access-token»\r\n

case:     a token cut short by an ellipsis
in:       pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789ab...
out:      pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789ab...

# Two tokens written together. No token can begin inside another: a token holds
# one dot, at its eighteenth character, and everything behind that dot is
# hexadecimal, which the p and the t of the prefix are not — so a token written
# inside one would want a dot where a secret stands, or would have to open on a
# p a secret cannot hold. The prefix written in front of a token, and an
# identifier carrying the prefix, are the two places a candidate does open
# inside a span, and neither becomes a token.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       pat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefpat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «airtable-personal-access-token»«airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     the prefix written in front of a token
in:       patpat0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pat«airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     an identifier opening on the prefix
in:       patpat0123456789a.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     an identifier closing on the prefix
in:       pat0123456789apat.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «airtable-personal-access-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. Sixty-four lowercase hexadecimal
# characters behind a seventeen character word and a dot is the vendor's format
# exactly, and a SHA-256 is sixty-four of them, so a word of that length in front
# of one is a token character for character and the whole of it goes. That is the
# answer rather than a fault in it, because nothing in the text tells such a run
# from a token: sparing it would spare a real token written the same way. The
# shorter digests are not secrets at any length, and neither is a UUID, whose
# hyphens are no character a secret may hold.

case:     a seventeen character word in front of a sha-256
in:       patchnotes1234567.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «airtable-personal-access-token»

case:     a sixteen character word in front of a sha-256
in:       patchnotes123456.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      patchnotes123456.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a seventeen character word in front of a sha-1
in:       patchnotes1234567.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      patchnotes1234567.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a seventeen character word in front of a uuid
in:       patchnotes1234567.01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      patchnotes1234567.01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The prefix is read in the case Airtable
# writes it and with every letter of it; an identifier of another kind is another
# thing Airtable numbers rather than a token; and a digest carries no dot, so
# none of them holds a candidate to be found at however long it runs.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       PAT0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      PAT0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the prefix without its closing letter
in:       pa0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pa0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an identifier of another kind
in:       usr0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      usr0123456789abcd.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a sha-256 with no identifier in front of it
in:       sha256=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      sha256=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     prose opening on the prefix
in:       the patch is on the path to the patient pattern
out:      the patch is on the path to the patient pattern

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a log line naming the api a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.airtable.com/v0/meta/whoami
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://api.airtable.com/v0/meta/whoami

# And the other access token Airtable issues, which this pattern has nothing to
# say about. An OAuth access token is written in four parts with .v1. between the
# first two, so its identifier is followed by a dot and a version rather than by
# a secret; Airtable calls it an OAuth access token where this is a personal
# access token, and it is a credential this pattern's name does not cover rather
# than one the scan happens to miss.

case:     an oauth access token
in:       oaa0123456789abcd.v1.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      oaa0123456789abcd.v1.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
